brief: Trump rejected Iran's proposed 7-day ceasefire that would have restored June 17 MOU conditions, after a WSJ report said he expects to resume bombing post-midterms but is reluctant to resume major operations now. The Iran War's impact on oil and rates has weighed on equity investor positioning and breadth: Goldman's Sentiment Indicator fell to -0.9, matching the March market low. AI strength has kept the S&P 500 headline resilient, but the median stock trades 16% below its 52-week high, pushing breadth to its lowest since the Dot-Com Bubble. Goldman reads this combination, weak positioning plus weak breadth, as pointing to potential for both broad market upside and a catch-up in laggards, conditional on macro uncertainty not accelerating. Prime brokerage data for the week: US L/S gross leverage rose 1.2 points to 210.6% (42nd percentile one-year), net leverage fell 1.2 points to 48.6% (5th percentile), and the fundamental long/short ratio fell 1.5% to 1.601 (3rd percentile). Global hedge funds gained 90bps, now +13% year to date. Single-stock short selling was the largest in three months (-2.2 SDs); seven of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Communication Services, Health Care, Energy, and Staples.
